page_text: A primitive axe that isn't very sturdy, but it gets the job done.

Chopping blocks can be used to cut wooden parts into smaller pieces.$(br2)Right click the item onto the chopping block, then right click the block with your axe several times until the item has been processed.

The worktable is a primitive version of the crafting table.$(br2)Items must be placed on the 9 slots by right-clicking them.$(br2)Once the correct items have been placed, use a $(l:basics/crude_hammer)hammer$() and right-click the top of the worktable to craft the item.
Sneaking while looking at an item inside a storage container shows how many of that item are available.$(br2)Using the scroll wheel while sneaking either adds or removes items.
Hammers have several uses, and the better the material, the longer they will last.

A basket can be placed in-world, or picked up with its contents.$(br)However, when picked up, it can only be placed inside the hotbar.$(br2)The bigger the basket, the more items and larger stacks it can hold.
title: Baskets

page_text: The pit kiln is an early and rough way of refining certain items and blocks.$(br)Place the pit kiln block inside a 1 deep and wide hole.$(br2)Right click the item you want to process (up to a stack of 8).$(br2)Place thatch and logs on top, then set it on fire.
The glass block represents any solid block
More complicated machines and blocks need to be created in an assembler.$(br2)These mechanical crafters require a minimum (and sometimes maximum) amount of rotational power to function.

One of the faces acts as the output, while the others act as the input.$(br2)Using hoppers or pipes, items can be piped into these slots.$(br2)The simple assmelber can only hold up to 4 different item types.$(br2)Right-click the assembler to select a recipe, otherwise it will craft whatever it can with the items available.
Rotational power is the main method of powering a lot of machinery.$(br2)There are several ways to achieve this, which will be laid out here as i discover them.

The earlierst form of rotational power can be achieved with windmills.$(br2)The higher these are placed, the faster they can spin, producing more power.$(br2)Additional blades can be attached to speed them up as well.

A ratiobox can transfer rotational power between windmill, axles, machines, etc.$(br2)Right-click any of it's faces with an axle to change the input/output mode.$(br2)Right-click it with an empty hand to specify its power distribution.
